rulings.restated: Enter the smaller of helper "State or local income tax refunds, credits or offsets you received in 2025" or helper "The amount on your 2024 Schedule A, line 5d".
rulings.model: Taking the smaller of the 1099-G refund and 2024 Schedule A line 5d matches the worksheet. But neither refusal covers three Pub. 525 exceptions: "You received a refund in 2025 that is for a tax year other than 2024", "You made your last payment of 2024 estimated state or local income tax in 2025", and the precondition that the refund be "for a tax you paid in 2024 and you deducted state and local income taxes on your 2024 Schedule A". The refund input counts every refund received in 2025, so those cases get computed here instead of being sent to Pub. 525.
rulings.ruling: Ruling: refusal located elsewhere; project retained. The cases named are refused on the line that reads this one: refund.taxable, which Schedule 1 line 1 enters, refuses on refund.not_2024 ("Is any of these refunds for a tax year other than 2024 (box 3 of Form 1099-G), or did you make your last payment of 2024 estimated state or local income tax in 2025?"), exceptions 1 and 5 (i1040gi p. 89, Line 1, "1. You received a refund in 2025 that is for a tax year other than 2024", "5. You made your last payment of 2024 estimated state or local income tax in 2025"), and gives zero, without the worksheet, unless you itemized for 2024 and deducted income rather than sales taxes (refund.worksheet; p. 88, Line 1, "If the refund was for a tax you paid in 2024 and you deducted state and local income taxes on your 2024 Schedule A, use the State and Local Income Tax Refund Worksheet"). Exceptions 3, 4 and 6 to 9 are the two refusals on this line (refund.exc_tax, refund.exc_who), exception 2 is refused by the Schedule 1 screen (scope.schedule1, which names other recoveries of amounts deducted or credited in an earlier year).

rulings.ruling: Ruling: scope; i1040gi p. 89, Line 1, Exception: "See Itemized Deduction Recoveries in Pub. 525 instead of using the State and Local Income Tax Refund Worksheet ... if any of the following applies", "1. You received a refund in 2025 that is for a tax year other than 2024" and "5. You made your last payment of 2024 estimated state or local income tax in 2025". Both are screened by refund.not_2024 ("Is any of these refunds for a tax year other than 2024 (box 3 of Form 1099-G), or did you make your last payment of 2024 estimated state or local income tax in 2025?"), whose refusal sits on refund.taxable, the line Schedule 1 line 1 enters, so no such refund reaches a completed return through line 1. The refusal is located on the reading line rather than line 1 itself; the model saw only line 1's two refusals (exc_tax, exc_who: items 3, 4, 6-9). The min with 2024 Schedule A line 5d matches ("But don't enter more than the amount of your state and local income taxes shown on your 2024 Schedule A, line 5d"). Same as the archived ruling, rechecked.

rulings.restated: Add helper "The amount for the box "You were born before January 2, 1960" (zero if not checked)", helper "The amount for the box "You are blind" (zero if not checked)", helper "The amount for the box "Spouse was born before January 2, 1960" (zero if not checked, and when your 2024 filing status was not married filing jointly or married filing separately)", and helper "The amount for the box "Spouse is blind" (zero if not checked, and when your 2024 filing status was not married filing jointly or married filing separately)".
rulings.model: The worksheet says 'Multiply the number of boxes checked by $1,550 ($1,950 if your 2024 filing status was single or head of household)'. The per-box amount helpers are not defined in the glossary, so the rate cannot be checked. The spouse-box gate (allowed only for MFJ/MFS) does not show the footnote condition for MFS: 'only if your spouse had no income, isn't filing a return, and can't be claimed as a dependent'. The worksheet text also gives no basis for zeroing spouse boxes for qualifying surviving spouse.
rulings.ruling: Ruling: representation; i1040gi p. 90, State and Local Income Tax Refund Worksheet, line 6: "Multiply the number of boxes checked by $1,550 ($1,950 if your 2024 filing status was single or head of household)". Each per-box helper is refund.per_box ("$1,550 ($1,950 if your 2024 filing status was single or head of household)": single/hoh -> refund.box_unmarried $1,950; mfj/mfs/qss -> refund.box_married $1,550) when its box is checked and zero otherwise, so the sum is boxes times the rate. The MFS footnote ("If your filing status is married filing separately, you can check the boxes for your spouse only if your spouse had no income, isn't filing a return, and can't be claimed as a dependent on another person's return") is carried in the spouse questions refund.spouse_born and refund.spouse_blind ("If your 2024 filing status was married filing separately, answer yes only if your spouse also had no income, wasn't filing a return, and couldn't be claimed as a dependent"). The rate was not checkable by the model because helpers are glossed only by label (the label does state the rate). On the qualifying-surviving-spouse point (spouse boxes zero unless 2024 status MFJ or MFS): ambiguity, amb.2025.refund_boxes_2024 (chosen reading: "ask the spouse questions only when the 2024 filing status was married filing jointly or married filing separately"); the worksheet is silent on QSS, and on the 2024 Form 1040 the spouse boxes belong to a spouse on the return.

rulings.ruling: Ruling: representation; project retained. Each per-box helper is refund.per_box when its box is checked and zero otherwise, and refund.per_box is $1,550, or $1,950 when the 2024 status was single or head of household (refund.box_married, refund.box_unmarried), so the sum is the number of boxes times the amount (i1040gi p. 90, State and Local Income Tax Refund Worksheet, line 6, "Multiply the number of boxes checked by $1,550 ($1,950 if your 2024 filing status was single or head of household)"). The married filing separately condition for the spouse boxes is in the spouse questions themselves (refund.spouse_born, refund.spouse_blind: "answer yes only if your spouse also had no income, wasn't filing a return, and couldn't be claimed as a dependent on another person's return"), as the footnote says ("you can check the boxes for your spouse only if your spouse had no income, isn't filing a return, and can't be claimed as a dependent"); amb.2025.refund_boxes_2024 records the reading.
